text: In the 11 years I have spent representing Scarborough Southwest, it has been commonplace for people to conduct post-funeral rites (e.g. scattering of ashes, etc.) along waterfront areas, including parts of Bluffer's Park. Conversations concerning such ceremonies have recently been brought to the forefront through coverage in various media outlets. Some park patrons have expressed environmental concerns regarding the disposal of non-decomposable materials associated with such ceremonies. Although I recognize the value of such concerns, I feel it is also important to recognize and respect that the scattering of ashes on water is a traditional practice for various cultures. I believe the key to balancing these interests is through studying the creation of designated areas to conduct such ceremonies. Clear models for this exist in other municipalities, such as Pickering and Mississauga, and…

City Council on May 5 and 6, 2021, adopted the following: 1. City Council direct the General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation to report to the May 25, 2021 meeting of Infrastructure and Environment Committee on the feasibility of creating designated areas for the scattering of ashes along the City's waterfront.
